The verse says: Who says the divine pearl anchors the ocean's edge? As soon as a thought arises, everything is amiss.
In vain has Sāgara toiled with diligent guarding; it fills the entire universe—this is all his.

Question: Before King Majestic Sound (Vaiśvānara-rāja), there was a pair of unperforated iron hammers. Why did the Great Compassionate One, whose body and hands were all eyes, search for them so thoroughly yet fail to find them?
The Master said: "When heard, it is as if one possesses great wealth; a single coin is not its equal. After seen, one is impoverished; ten thousand pieces of gold cannot buy it."
The verse says: At the base of Mount Sumeru lies the universal vajra; it penetrates the seas and pierces through the mountains, radiating light everywhere.
Only a wild monk here and there can pulverize it; few in the human realm or heavens are capable of taking it up.
Question: "Puhua constantly performs somersaults at all times; I wonder, what kind of intention does he have?
The Master said: "He has no good intentions at all. It is easy to gain fat for the sides, but it is difficult to find flesh for the belly."
The verse says: Having obtained the true essence of Panshan through the brush as its cause, he understands how to perform somersaults throughout the monasteries.
The world calls him mad; on the precious lotus throne, he laughs "he-he. Laughing at what? At a live flea!
Question: An ancient worthy said, "If you have a staff, I give you a staff; if you have no staff, I take away your staff.
Since there is no staff, what is there to take away?
The Master said: "To seize it from his hand while it is bottomless is to see his true skill.
He then offered this verse: Severing the many white clouds atop the mountain peak, The clear breeze can do nothing but glare with both eyes.
If one could gather up empty flowers and mirages, How many would there be to bring them back?
Question: "The Baguī Hermit waits at the crossroads for someone to come.
I do not know what kind of intention this old man has.
The Master said: "I shall tell you when you have waited for him to arrive."
The verse says: A single person comes, alone and unaccompanied; who perceives that this person has long been within the breast?
A pity for the wandering travelers from all quarters, who exhaust their spiritual powers and mental efforts in vain conjecture.
Question: When Shitou asked Nanyue, "One does not admire the various sages, nor does one prize one's own spiritual brilliance;
it would be better to undergo perpetual sinking and delusion than to seek liberation from the various sages. Why is this so?
The Master said, "Alas! What need is there for such a stubborn fellow?
He then offered this verse: "The Vairambha wind holds fast the one world of heaven and earth; The myriad phenomena and all that exists are already in accord.
This is the scope of Gautama’s gathering and releasing; Root and sprout continue on, preserved until this day."
Question: When Baizhang went for his second visit to Mazu, he encountered Mazu’s single shout, which left him with deaf ears for three days.
After becoming deaf, what did he obtain?
The Master said: "That which Śākyamuni Buddha entrusted to Kāśyapa."
The verse says: A crossbow of a thousand *jin* is not for a field mouse; with a single stroke of its tip, it subdues the majesty of the lion.
When dragons and elephants behold it, their hearts and gallbladders shatter; it is truly a marvel in both the world and the heavens.
Question: The Dharma is that which all Buddhas preach; for what reason, then, do all Buddhas take the Dharma as their teacher? I venture to ask:
before the Buddhas were born, where did the Dharma abide?
The Master raised his whisk and said, "Do you understand? This is the teacher of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. He then spoke a verse:
Among the multitude there is no guest from Cold Mountain; Never speak a single word with such a person.
In days of yore, Danxia lacked the power of transformation; He would certainly have called him a madman.
Question: "Do not say that 'no-mind' is itself the Way; no-mind still leaves one separated by a further barrier. I do not know what this barrier is.
The Master said: "This very one is unmistakable. To realize it and yet add further conceptualization is like adding a wooden yoke to a head already bare."
The Verse says: The upright Han people have never been deceived from of old; I have never raised a thought without them knowing it beforehand.
Even the vast heavens understand the intentions of men, How much more so the Teacher who guides gods and humans?
Question: Bodhidharma came from the West pointing directly to the human mind, so that by seeing one's nature one becomes a Buddha.
Why, then, did Zhaozhou also say, "I do not like to hear the single word 'Buddha'?"
The Master said: "A thief will never admit to being a thief; when the evidence is exposed, one cannot contest it.
The verse says: "Gānjiāng will by no means yield to injustice; Yet whoever meets him at the front will suffer injury.
When the whole world hears of his reputation, they will surely be struck with fear; What joy is there in rolling three heads together?"
Question: "To protect living beings, one must kill; only when they are all killed can one dwell in peace.
For a practitioner of the Way, where is compassion? The Master said: "Excellent! The petty man is distracted by external appearances; the superior man is cautious in his solitude."

The verse says: Ninefold enclosures guard the majesty of Heaven; By imperial decree, they circulate throughout the nine regions. They exterminate rebels, eliminate the treacherous, and destroy the deceitful and sycophantic;
In implementing governance and issuing policies, they act according to the exigencies of the times.
Question: "The ancients had a certain unresolved koan. I ask the Master to resolve it for me; it would be well to spare people from having to carry it on their lips and teeth.
The Master said: "It is perfectly fine to bring it up; it will dissolve like ice melting or a wall collapsing."
The verse says: Grasping the mouth of the central cloth bag, who would fear a thousand or ten thousand heads?
Coarse and fine, holy and ordinary, all are gathered within; let them be joyful or sorrowful—it matters not.
A question was asked: "In ancient times, after drawing a circle and presenting it, they performed a woman’s bow. Looking at this now, what kind of atmosphere is this?
The Master said: "The flower was held up to the assembly; who could understand that smile?"
The verse says: A beautiful lady with rouge and powder continues the ancestral lamp; the courtesan at the sands of Jinshe.
In both the human realm and the heavens, she alone is honored as supreme. How could such as these ever be counted among the duality?
Question: "In ancient times, an old man was playfully striking the earth with a mallet when the earth shattered and he attained great enlightenment. I do not know where this enlightenment lay.
The Master struck the sounding block once and said, "A hundred pieces of miscellaneous fragments."
The verse says: Sporting in samādhi, they form groups and bands; they seize the nostrils with painful grip. From one repentance to another, they continue in remorse.
They stride across the five sacred peaks in carefree leisure; they shatter the vajra, and their single body is noble and wealthy.
A single *zhilu* staff is as lively as a dragon; ten thousand acres of blue waves all hold their breath.
Question: "The ancients wrote the character for 'mind' (心) upon the walls of their gates; what was their intention? The Master said:
"Reclining on pines and rocks when there is nothing to do; hanging up a signboard to practice divination."

The verse says: One must not sell one's heart or liver for the sake of others. Advancing further from the top of a hundred-foot pole, If you penetrate the true intent of the ancients, You will roam freely throughout the world, outwitting Heaven itself.
Question: The teachings state that if one can "turn" objects, one is identical to the Tathāgata. Suppose there were Mount Sumeru—how would one turn it?
The Master said: "Tsk! Gather it up and place it within the pore of a mustard seed."
The verse says: A single speck of dust, a single seat, a five-flower pedestal; the Dharma-preaching spreads like clouds across the nine realms.
Yet strange patch-robed monks do not perceive it at all; why need they transform objects to be like the Tathāgata?
Question: When Dajue visited Linji, Linji held up his whisk; Dajue spread out his sitting cloth. Linji threw down the whisk;
Dajue gathered up his sitting cloth and departed. I venture to ask: what kind of eye did he possess that he did not prostrate himself before leaving?
The Master said: "Guangmi meets Bodhidharma. The verse says:
Without raising an eyebrow, he already knows; Opening the door, he remembers the moment of closing it. The dragon soars and clouds arise as teacher and disciple unite;
The tiger roars and the wind arises as guest and host return home.
Question: Under Mazu, there were over eighty enlightened teachers (sanzhishi), yet only three or five attained the Patriarch’s True Dharma Eye.
Even Niu Tou was reportedly unaware of the "upper pivot. How far apart, then, are this pivot and the True Dharma Eye?
The Master said: "Tsk! Exit through the main gate for now; do not pass through the patriarch’s barrier. He spoke in verse:
"The Gan and Xiang rivers wind through eighteen bends; As the boat travels, those before and behind lean against one another. Though they are thus separated, there is no hindrance;
Upon reaching the shore, all is pure and secluded, equally at ease."
Question: "Shifting one's expression reveals the ancient path; one does not fall into the silent mechanism. It is further said: "On the ancient path, a venomous snake wears horns upon its head.
What is this "ancient path"?
The Master said: "Tsk! Walking crookedly, it is difficult to set foot down;
you have not yet realized the source. He spoke in verse: "A path exists in every house leading to Chang'an; Before arriving, many are surely deceived by others.
Once one is accustomed to it, heaven and earth are but a single eye; Let his words be as numerous as a hundred thousand kinds."
Question: "All sentient beings, from the wriggling insects upward, possess Buddha-nature. I venture to ask the World-Honored One: before you appeared in the world, did the Buddha-dharma exist or not?
The Master rebuked him, saying: "Those who understand speak in the marketplace; those who do not understand speak at home."

The verse says: "Every thing grows in summer and is born in spring; every person stands head toward heaven and feet upon earth. Whether it be existence or non-existence, know the mind and know yourself.
Question: "If a ruler of the Way does not accept wise ministers, and you, Master, are advanced in years, do you still require attendants?"
[The Master] said: "No. The Teacher said: "Hmph! You must indeed employ him; do not allow him to draw near. He spoke in verse:
"Dwelling alone in the Dharma-realm, he is called solitary; In the jeweled palace, all is still—there is not a single thing. He benefits all beings and brings them profit."
Do not harbor constant fear. Do not teach people to prostrate before the Buddha Vairocana.
Question: If you say this is it, you are adding a head atop a head; if you say it is not, you are cutting off your head to seek life.
"How, in the end, can one reach home?
The Master said, "Seeing injustice on the road, draw the sword to assist.
The Verse says: "The blade of the Great Axe emerges from its scabbard; it is mostly for cutting away what is unjust. When both sides are unified as one, the Middle Way..."
Do not let it become emaciated. Do not trouble yourself with disputes over quantity; there is no need to seek proof for right or wrong.
Even those with three heads and six arms are not permitted to enter the central hall.
Question: When Zhaozhou was traveling on pilgrimage to the south, he arrived at the head of a brazier and encountered the "guestless host" koan. This continued until—
"Now there is no one to raise this up; I request the Master to raise it.
The Master rebuked him, saying, "The younger generation has many tomorrows; the old man has mostly passed times. He then spoke in verse:
"The light of the eyes pierces through the four worlds; It shall never again allow people to walk in darkness. There was neither guest nor host.
"I have finished my work," he said. "I do not know how many people I have caused to fall and be killed.
A monk asked, "I ask Master Tong'an: What is the Teacher of Gods and Men? An replied, "The horns upon his head are incomplete;
the hair upon his body does not emerge. What is the meaning of this?
The Master said: "Aha! Having a mouth but no mind, his speech is most true. He then offered this verse:
"Walking among those of different species, he manifests world-transcending wonders; The four modes of birth pass away, for he has no dependence on them at all.
He is the Teacher of Gods and Humans, yet even this is not what makes him noble; His hair and horns are empty, and he understands how to fly."
Question: Master Dahui said, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have been swallowed by me in a single gulp;
where else could there be sentient beings left to deliver? Why, then, did he leave behind Amitābha and Avalokiteśvara?"
The Master raised his ruler and said, "Heh! Today, Sizha has met my hand.
He spoke in verse: "The Buddhas of the three periods were swallowed by him; Now he, in turn, suddenly meets my hand.
I shall reduce this one-foot ruler to fine dust, Causing the Dharma-way of Amitābha to endure for long."
Question: "To exhaust the void and pervade the Dharma-realm—this is the wisdom of Mañjuśrī and the practice of Samantabhadra.
I wonder, within the sphere of the patch-robed monk, what is it like?"
The Master said: "Eh! It pervades and encompasses empty space; it contains the Dharma-realm at all times. He then spoke in verse:
"At times there are the myriad phenomena, at times there is emptiness; Hell and heaven are not passageways through which one travels.
Such is the natural state, not a product of fabrication; Even the Three Worthies and Ten Sages find their spirits startled."
Question: Puhua shook his bell, Heshan struck the drum, Shigong drew his bow, and Kāśyapa performed a dance.
Do such maneuvers as these suffice for the School of the Patriarchs?
The Master said: "If you seek blessings in the heavens, you must employ the wealth of this world.
He spoke in verse: "The old man preaching the Dharma is too lazy to open his mouth; He merely causes the drums, bells, bows, and arrows to run about.
When those with wisdom meet him, they do not knit their brows; When the heartless encounter him, he frequently beckons with his hand."
Question: "The stone ox bellows loudly beyond the void; the wooden horse neighs occasionally before the bright moon. I wonder, who is it that enjoys this?
The Master said, "As for this matter, I, an old monk, truly do not know."
The verse says: This person is strange and extraordinary, with no known origin; he dwells neither within heaven and earth nor among the nine schools of thought.
He cannot be retained even within the ranks of Buddhas and patriarchs; how could ten thousand schemes and stratagems ever capture him?

Question: When the inhalation does not dwell within the aggregates and realms, and the exhalation does not involve the manifold conditions, one constantly turns this sutra hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of times. What, then, is this sutra that does not turn?
The Master said: "The Brahma-sound is profound and wondrous, causing people to delight in hearing it.
He spoke in verse: "The hands do not let go of the scroll, yet there are no characters; The three baskets of the precious cases are proclaimed from a single mouth.
Had it not been for the Sage King’s ability to possess the eye of discernment, It would have been a near thing had the entire assembly failed to vindicate their grievance."
Question: Han Yu asked the same question of both Dadian and the Head Seat; Dadian and the Head Seat gave identical answers.
Why, then, did he refuse to accept the Head Seat?
The Master said, "Hmph! Do not misunderstand this; it is simply that the Head Seat did not approve of Dadian.
He then offered this verse: "Examining whether the various quarters are the same or different, Sometimes he appears in the west, sometimes in the east.
If Master Wen had possessed the eyes of Mahesvara, How could he have been willing to leave his robes behind for the Great Public?"
Question: Master Xiu’s verse says, "All Buddha-dharma is inherently present within one's own mind; to seek it elsewhere with the mind is to abandon one's father and run away.
Now tell me, what is this inherently present Buddha-dharma?
The Master said: "Alas! What words are these? Zong has obtained the family inheritance, yet he cannot avoid running away.

He then offered this verse: "The Sage Ruler weaves his governance; both within and without are at peace. How could the defense and protection reside merely in the Golden Pavilion? Generations of hereditary rank are not what is truly noble;
Only the one who yields his preeminence and topples the *chatravala* (the banner-pole) is truly victorious."
A question was asked: "I have long heard that National Teacher Zhong left behind a 'seamless stupa.
Where is it located right now? The Master said: "Tsk! The iron ox of Shanzhou has fallen into a pile of manure. Go and look for it!"
The verse says: For a long time I have admired the pagoda of Nanyang; throughout the world, no one has known how to seek it out.
At that time, Xuedou pointed to a shadow; to this day, those across the lakes and seas continue to ponder it in vain.
Question: "The Buddhas of the three periods do not preach the Dharma; the patriarchs of successive generations do not practice Chan.
Tell me, who is it that can go in such a way?
The Master said: "One who is blind, deaf, and mute."
The verse says: Exhausting the pivot and mechanism of the world, certainty never deviates; square and round, left and right—how wondrous and marvelous!
Before every gate lies a road that reaches through the night; why then go to the street corner to ask a fool?
Question: All Buddhas and Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi emerge from this sutra.
Tell me, what is this sutra?
The Master said: "Learning is the foremost. The verse says:
Step by step, turn after turn, all is perfectly clear; Why need one spend three years explaining the causes?
The myriad phenomena and the ten thousand forms manifest together; Vain seekers only moisten their own collars with tears.
Question: "If no Buddhas appear in the world, may I ask who it is that descends from the royal palace to preach the Dharma and benefit sentient beings?
The Master said: "A hitching post for donkeys."

The Verse says: From the beginning, news of this has never been permitted to be known; Yet for some reason, the celestial mechanism has been leaked once more. The Great Void contains heaven and earth throughout past and present;
As for birth and death, the true and the mundane—who can say who they are?
Question: The *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* states: "If one person awakens to the truth and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions will all vanish away.
Since time immemorial until the present, those who have attained the Way are as numerous as hemp seeds and millet grains; why then do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth never undergo change?
The Master said, "Eh! Yet another cataract has arisen. He spoke in verse:
"With eyes intact, one naturally discerns the right from the wrong; From that void, empty flowers arise.
The pearls have already been gathered within the pouch; Let the blind man do as he pleases and scatter sand at will."
Question: The Prince Nanda split his bones to return them to his father and his flesh to return them to his mother;
thereafter, he manifested his original body to preach the Dharma to his parents. What is this "original body" of Nanda?
The Master said: "Tsk! I permit you to see it, but I do not permit others to hear it.
He then spoke this verse: "The true gold from the great furnace never changes its color; As vessels fashioned according to their form, they are beyond measure.
Once encountered by the furnace and bellows, they are melted into unity; Ten thousand shapes and a thousand forms—nowhere can they be hidden."
Question: “The boundless ocean of lands is not separated from the tip of a single hair. May I ask whether the Brahma King and Śakra Devendra are likewise contained within that same space?
The Master said: “One must consult with the Persian interpreter before one can understand.”
The verse says: Contemplating the infinite oceans of lands as a single essence—what need is there to further discuss a single hair-tip?
From between his brows protrudes the eye of Mahesvara; he is not deceived by the traces of the realms of the true or the mundane.
Question: "The Buddha knows the events of the causal stage throughout immeasurable kalpas. I ask the Master:
do you still remember what happened three lifetimes ago? The Master replied: "I have just told you."
The verse says: This single moment pervades all kalpas; past, present, and future, throughout the three periods of time, are contained within a single speck of dust.
Space may come to an end, but this channel remains inexhaustible. Raise your eyebrows—do they coincide, or do they differ?
Question: "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, in what place shall one find a dwelling and establish one's life?
The Master said: "Look within the flames—who is this?"
The verse says: When the clouds of doubt have completely dispersed, the golden sun is revealed; when the seas and mountains are empty and luminous, existence and non-existence are mirrored.
Let the ashes of kalpas be scattered until nothing remains; remain upright and unmoved, untouched by the red-bearded barbarian.
A questioner asked, "To have precious wealth filling one's room is not noble; it is better to relieve the poor and succor the destitute.
I request that you, Master, grant me a small portion of alms for my daily sustenance.
The Master said, "Come closer and take it. If you give rise to the thought of receiving a gift, you will inevitably still have something left to attend to."
The Verse says: Drinking from mountain streams and eating pine needles, his resolve is uniquely lofty; How can he be compared to those old masters of *fengsao* who strive for mere eccentricity?
Fushan personally provided the five flavors to the assembly; How could the monastery’s permanent provisions have ever been diminished by even a hair’s breadth?
Question: "The capacity exists because of the object; the object sinks as it pursues the capacity. When both capacity and object are forgotten, what is this thing?
The Master said: "It has a name but no reality; it is reality, not a name."
The verse says: To divide the smoke and split the cooking fires is most difficult to do; to unite and maintain a household is extremely easy to sustain.
Filial piety and harmony accord with the will of Heaven; when things are most convenient, few people realize it.
Question: "One who wears the yellow cap and feathered cloak, riding on mists and walking amidst the void, is not called a 'Way-man' (daoren).
May I ask, who then is a Way-man? The Master said: "Do you recognize this old gentleman here? He is the Teacher of the Three Pure Ones."
The verse says: The Daoist does not ride cranes or mount clouds; how could he dwell on Penglai or in the Great Clarity?
With its jade grasses, vermilion flowers, and palaces of precious jade—such things are merely objects for the mind to crave and fall into, like a wild fox spirit.
Question: Even if one fully wields the orthodox command, it is merely playing with the head of a dead snake; even if the bright moon is in the sky, one is still but a man standing at the steps.
What is it like to be a person of the higher realm?
The Master said: "One who does not wear sandals for wandering through clouds and waters will not deign to don the jeweled flower crown.
He then offered this verse: "The falling raindrops are all gathered up at once; I alone admire the venerable monk Lingyun.
He established his school with boundless measure; Those who merely step upon it find themselves as if facing an enemy."
Question: We have heard the Master say, "Mount Sumeru shatters and forms into a ball. We do not question its forming into a ball;
but where has Śakra gone at this very moment?
The Master said: "Aha! Look within your own eyes!
He then offered this verse: If one’s vision is not penetrating and one’s questioning is not thorough, why should one body further serve many mothers?
One who thoroughly understands that which is illusory and unborn may split open a walnut; nothing at all is hindered.
Question: "Last night, my question was already presented to the Abbot long ago. For what reason, Master, do you not grant me a response?
The Master said: "It shall be so. He then spoke in verse:
"The jade branches, inch by inch, are precious treasures; The liquid from the deep waters, drop by drop, is wondrous fragrance. The place of jewels is certain."
However, lacking the necessary implements, one cannot digest this through the idle deliberations of the conscious mind.
Question: An ancient worthy said, "The single word 'enlightenment' must be spat out. I venture to ask the Old Monk: have you spat it out or not?
The Master said: "Tsk! The moon has the intention to delight in the deep pool, yet the water has no heart to cherish the moon.
He spoke in verse: "The Great Man and the Noble Person maintain a mind of equanimity; They do not reject the ignorant, nor do they exalt the perverse.
If you wish to have a single thread of connection with me, Do not travel to Mount Nanyue or Mount Tiantai."
Question: "When Master Nianhua commanded the assembly to clear the fields and permitted the exposition of the Great Meaning, why did he merely extend both hands when he ascended the hall?
The Master said: "Heh! To seek meaning apart from the field—the arrow has long since flown past."
The verse says: Vast and boundless, a single expanse of white waves reaching to the heavens; how could the Great Meaning ever have been incomplete?
From this moment, one understands how to turn the body and cast off the shell, soaring beyond the world, free from all triviality.
Question: Guishan called out to Yangshan, saying, "Huiji. Huiji responded, "Yes. Guishan said, "He has come forth. At this, Yangshan attained great enlightenment.
However, it was not yet known what exactly he had awakened to.
The Master said, "Hmph! The well-rope has snapped; the pain is unbearable. He then offered this verse:
"The Qilin falls into the weeds and can do nothing about it; Suddenly meeting one who leads it out, it becomes at ease.
A single gāthā heals that which lies beyond kalpas; Know that each possesses its own favorable conditions."
Question: When Muzhou closed the gate and Yunmen injured his foot, he attained great enlightenment. Ultimately, what did he realize?
The Master said: "Tsk! To cry out and stir up dreams is a matter of many complications."
The verse says: To be a person, one must act until reaching the ultimate; to kill a person, one must certainly see the blood.
As long as there is a breath of life, it will create an obstacle; when pressed against a precipice, the life-root is severed.
Question: Wansong said of Luopu, "It was like inserting a stiff key into an old lock; having already eaten the salt and vinegar of everyday life, he knew their sourness.
Thereupon, he took these words to heart. Where is that key now?
The Master struck him with a one-chi staff and said, "Where is it gathered and released?
He then offered this verse: Wearing thin sandals, he traveled the roads of India; A withered vine snapped through the clouds of sea and mountains.
When the wax-plum blossoms have fallen away in the empty valley, He smiles as he gazes upon the Southern Mountain revealing the early spring.
Question: When Mazu ascended the hall, Baizhang rolled up his mat; what kind of eye did he possess that he would not allow the Master to preach the Dharma?
The Master said: "Tsk! It was only right that it should be so. There was no need for further delay."
The verse says: It was only because the nostrils were pierced through with pain that the resentment in one’s heart for a lifetime could not be extinguished.
Having seized the essential pass and letting nothing escape, there is yet another state of carefree wandering beyond this carefree wandering.
Question: "The Hermitage Master’s raising of his fist was no different from [the Buddha’s] response. What was Zhaozhou’s intent in both praising and disparaging him?
The Master said: "When boundaries are strictly enforced, one is not permitted to cut in line or seize the market."
The verse says: Pointing south to find the celestial mechanism—when you look up, you will surely not know it.
If you can understand it before the words end and after they begin, it will be as difficult to pursue as a flash of lightning or a spark from flint.
Question: Master Fu said, "He is the lord of the myriad phenomena, yet he does not wither along with the four seasons.
Yet now, there is sprouting in spring, growth in summer, killing in autumn, and withering in winter. Is there, within this, anyone who acts as the true lord?
The Master said: "This concerns the Year-Head.
He spoke in verse: Each person has their own primordial ancestor; Lift your eyebrows, there is no need to look.
The myriad phenomena and the ten thousand things are hidden within; Their distinct features are clear—do not try to deceive yourself.
Question: Linji said, "Upon this ball of red flesh there is a true person of no rank; those who have not yet attained realization, look!
A monk asked, "What is the true person of no rank? Linji seized him and said, "Speak! Speak!
As the monk hesitated, Linji said, "The true person of no rank—what a dried-up shit-stick! How is the principle of this to be understood?
The Master said: "It is like a lion seizing a rabbit, exhausting all its prowess.
He then offered this verse: "Rowing a boat without reaching the shore, It kills the person on the bank with vexation. He is much like a thief who steals in broad daylight;
Only the deaf may be permitted to know his music."
A questioner asked, "I have caught a wild fox spirit; does it not violate the Master’s taboo name?
The Master said, "Ei! Dare you say it is not just a dead cat?"
The verse says: "Is this not a wild fox capable of transformation? With its golden fur, it enters the ranks and its heart knows no fear.
Bring it here, open its mouth, and let me hear; I shall certainly not fail to distinguish its truth from its falsehood."
Question: "When I was not yet ordained, I had a question that no one has been able to answer until now. I request that the Master answer it. The Master said:
"I have already finished teaching the nine middle sons about this; you may ask them yourself. Otherwise, the seven younger sons would be better suited to answer."
The verse says: When enemies meet, their brows knit together; each knows it in his heart—what need for words?
Since there is no letting go, what can be given? A foot across the head, and another punch on top.
Question: "A white heron descends to the field—a thousand dots of snow; a yellow oriole perches on a tree—a single branch of blossoms.
May I ask whose realm this is? The Master said: "Hmph! What a pack of beasts, capable of such antics!"
The verse says: The realm of the Chan school transcends all causes and conditions; Scattered trees and spread fields need not be sought.
Today one has already attained the face of a Bodhisattva; Yesterday morning was originally the heart of a yakṣa.
Question: An ancient said, "Wait until the stone tortoise nods its head, and I shall tell you. Now, the stone tortoise has nodded its head; how do you speak?
The Master said: "Eh! The frogs croak in a cacophony; it is also called the sound of the *jingban* board.
He then offered this verse: "The turning of the body and the continuity of the phrase follow through; A far-reaching, linked chain, a wind that has vibrated since antiquity.
Only after one has ripped open the heart, intestines, liver, and gallbladder Does the Old Barbarian fail to understand the Shaolin School."
Question: Fenyang asked Shoushan, "What is the meaning of Baizhang’s rolling up the mat? Shou said, "The dragon’s sleeve is swept aside, and the whole body is revealed;
where the Elephant King walks, there is no trace of the fox. Fenyang attained great enlightenment. [The questioner] asks: What did he realize?
The Master said: "Tsk! This is merely a hound chasing after a clod of earth.
The verse says: "A thousand-year-old scrap of paper is good for compounding medicine; it only requires a Physician King who understands the prescriptions.
If one bestows a fortune of a million households, there is no need for written contracts to be a worthy person."

Question: "The teachings of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the canon, as well as the one thousand seven hundred cases of the [Chuanxin] Fa, are all merely yellow leaves used to stop a child's crying.
I venture to ask the Master: what is it that you preach?"
The Master said: "Eh! Let the deaf hear it; let the mute transmit it. He then offered this verse:
A fine steed chasing the wind needs no whip; What use is a coin to stop a child’s crying?
When the time comes, the staff becomes a dragon; When fortune turns, gold turns into bricks.
Question: "The Way belongs neither to knowing nor to not-knowing. Knowing is deluded awareness; not-knowing is the indeterminate (avyākṛta). How, then, can one attain accord with it? The Master said:
"Not realizing there is a film over the eye, you instead resent the flowers appearing in the sky."
The verse says: An infant desires only to taste milk and cream; who cares whether his own mother is not his mother?
Only when the day comes that he gains the eye of wisdom will every particle of dust and every world-realm manifest in their full glory.
Question: “Sleeping soundly at the crossroads of the city; flipping over at the bottom of a thousand-fathom sea—what use is such a person?
The Master said: “Tsk! To see something as strange and not take it as strange—that strangeness will destroy itself.”
The verse says: To understand and turn toward the Buddha while acting with contempt—this will surely result in a rebirth as a beast.
By day and under the blue sky one sleeps; at the third watch of the night one lingers on. These strange and eccentric descendants of the Śākyas have left the world in darkness until this very day.
Question: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are all sealed by a single dharma. What is this one dharma?
The Master said: "It is precisely these mountains, rivers, the great earth, the grasses, trees, and forests."
The verse says: Seeing, hearing, knowing, and perceiving are most dim; the myriad phenomena and all spirits are within the palm of one's hand.
If you do not enter the abode of the white clouds, how can you know that beneath your feet there is a pure breeze?
Question: When Ganxing was serving congee at Nanquan, he invited Nanquan to recite prayers.
Nanquan then struck the gavel and said, "I ask the assembly to recite the Mahāprajñāpāramitā for the sake of the marten and the white ox. Ganxing brushed his sleeves and departed.
Upon hearing this, Nanquan immediately smashed the cauldron. What does this mean?
The Master said: "Tsk! One gallops across the sea to subdue the East; the other sweeps across the heavens to bring back the North.
He then offered this verse: "By circumstance they encounter a mortal enemy; In their coming and going, their private and public conduct, how could they allow him to interfere?

This one brandishes a horizontal iron spear; that one presses down a golden seal. Again, he brushes his sleeves and departs; the hook has its bait. The cauldron is broken, yet the jade remains flawless."
Question: A monk came to visit Nanquan while he was staying in a hermitage. Nanquan said, "I am going up the mountain to do some work;
you cook some rice for yourself, eat it, and then bring me some. After the monk had cooked the rice and eaten it, he smashed all the cooking utensils. Nanquan returned in the afternoon.
He saw a monk sleeping on a bed, so Quan also lay down beside him. The monk immediately got up and left. "What is the principle behind this? [The Master] said:
"It is precisely for those who act as companions that one is born; it is for those who act as true friends that one dies."
The verse says: In all the world there has been none like the appearance of a true son; Indeed, the foul breath has spread in every direction.
Had Nanquan not relied on others to act, He would have surely given a beating inside the hermitage.
Question: If there is even a single dharma, Vairocana falls among ordinary beings; if there are no myriad dharmas, Samantabhadra loses his realm.
Since neither side is correct, how should a practitioner of the teachings proceed?
The Master said: "Seeing the jaw behind the head—do not associate with such.
He then offered this verse: Suddenly one has arrived at the Dharma King’s palace; What need is there to concern oneself with thousands or ten thousands of differences?
The sixteen-foot golden body is used like common grass; Nirvana and afflictions are both but empty flowers.
Question: "In the teachings, the *Chao* explains the *Shu*, and the *Shu* explains the *Jing*. I do not yet understand what the *Jing* explains.
The Master said: "HŪṂ! One person drags down two; three people drag down four."
The verse says: Interlocking rings, intricately entwined, cannot be extended or stretched; a single aperture is empty and penetrating, yet even that "one" does not exist.
This matter is not obtained from others; it is what Dharma originally pointed toward.
Question: "There is no Maitreya above in heaven; there is no Maitreya below in the earth. Ultimately, where does he dwell?
The Master said: "Heh! The brazier trembles, and sweat flows from my entire body."
The verse says: When Maitreya descends to be born in the future, every person will fall into a deep pit.
Now, within the Inner Court of Tuṣita, you are white-washing your own cage. In the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā*, there is no person and no self;
in the *Avataṃsaka* Dharma-realm, there is neither west nor east. The hearth-fire stirs—what can be done? You must know that there is clarity in unloading the boat.
Feng asked, "I have two hundred questions; I request that the Master provide a single sentence in response.
The Master said, "Aha! Have you even answered yet? It may be easy to turn one's body around, but it is difficult to speak from the very essence of one's being."
The verse says: A single phrase answers the question of the heavens; throughout antiquity and today, every inquiry regarding the teachings has been met with response.
If you still seek further traces of the mind’s path, it remains upright for a foot’s length and will not cease.
Question: When the bhikṣuṇī Utpalavarṇā saw the Buddha, the Buddha rebuked her, saying: "How can you bypass the great assembly of monks to see me?
Though you see my physical body (rūpakāya), you do not yet see my Dharma-body (dharmakāya). Yet Subhūti, while sitting in meditation in his mountain cave, was able to see my Dharma-body.
I do not understand where the benefit or the harm lies in this.
The Master said: "A sincere heart receives no good reward; for the Great Matter, there is no cause for sorrow.
He spoke in verse: "The tongue has bone, yet it is not the Buddha; Speech is without cause, yet it is the truth.
Whether one sees or does not see, all people are but a foot apart; Let him grind his bones to repay the Master’s kindness."
Question: Zhaozhou said, "I have finished reciting the entire Tripitaka. The old woman replied, "Why have you only recited half the Tripitaka?
What kind of eye did the old woman possess?
Master [Linji] said, "Wrong! Why so much talk?"
The verse says: One who possesses the eye can barely receive the offered money; he uses it extensively and frugally, yet does not act out of stinginess.
He has recited the Tripiṭaka once over and possesses many additional volumes; why, then, do you still say that his turning [of the wheel] is not yet complete?
Question: Dizang said to Fayen, "If one discusses the Buddha-dharma, everything is already fully realized. At these words, Fayen attained great enlightenment.
It is not known what it was that he awakened to.
The Master said: "A single stroke [of the brush] opens the eight characters; one enters directly with total clarity. He then offered this verse:
"A full platter is presented, pure and sweet nectar; Upon reaching the mouth, it causes life to perish instantly.
Having died and then revived again—this cannot be deceived; Yet I sigh in regret that at the crossroads, people vainly search for the sheep."
Praise to Amitābha: Homage to Amitābha!

It is like the bliss of the Third Dhyāna Heaven—how many can avoid being deceived by such things that cheat the sages and delude the common folk? How many can withstand this superficiality?
Shouchang, with great courage, speaks out directly: do not recklessly grasp at empty space. If there is anyone who commits the sin of using a *zhilu* staff [to strike], I shall certainly...
I personally accept this responsibility. Why? Because when meeting on a narrow path, one cannot avoid it. Śākyamuni praises the Yellow-Faced Old Man;
O Yellow-Faced Old Man, do not deceive me! You manifested as a white elephant to descend into the royal palace and took birth through Māyā.
Thus he became a mere failure. From birth until his final journey, he spoke whatever came to mind; for seventy-nine years he craved fame, and for forty-nine years he labored with bitter words.
At the end of his life, he could do nothing against the Old Man Yama; holding a *dharma-flower* in his hand, he asked the elders, "What do you say?
The elders replied, "It is well. Kāśyapa merely knitted his brows. Therefore, it cannot be put into words; one can only smile faintly. This has been transmitted in succession.
It was transmitted to the old monk, who emptied out a full measure of it for him. *Duḥ!* The Great Being’s gate is the Great Being’s realm;

throughout every land, the Dharma-realm is not separated by so much as a single speck of dust. To even conceive of paying homage with a focused mind— *Note: "Kao-lao" (栲栳) refers to a large wicker basket or measure used for grain.*
There is no sinew within the eye. Where is the fish basket on the sands of Jinnasha? The flat rock remains upon Potalaka Cliff.
If you see Avalokiteśvara in this place, gold dust falling into the eye will surely injure the pupil. Ultimately, how is it? The green mountains are secluded and profound;
the white clouds are deep.
Dharma Master Bodhidharma did not follow human sentiment; he gouged out hollows from good flesh and applied needles to the most painful spots.

When Emperor Wu of Liang posed a question regarding the primary principle (*paramārtha*), there was a vast silence and no answer—how perfectly clear! Yet [Bodhidharma] himself merely said, "I do not know. Truly, this is black.
A face as black as ink. For nine years he faced the wall, seeking that one person; after Shen Guang’s three prostrations, his mind was finally at peace.
With his single shoe he returned west, becoming a captive envoy for the Wei state. Up to the present day—alas! It is a pity that people miss the mark right before their own faces.
If it were the lame Yunmen, he would have struck him with a staff and fed him to a dog, so as to ensure peace throughout the world.
Eulogy for Chan Master Gu Mei of Yangshan:

Gu Mei, Gu Mei! What a monstrous marvel! Having received the grace of the Tathāgata, he continues the lineage of Linji. Employing the Diamond Circle, he shouts at the patriarchs and rebukes the founders;
with his palm, he strikes the wild fox spirits and rolls up their robes and coverlets. At times, he directs the ghosts and spirits to act upon Mount Yang.
The wind. Or perhaps, relying on lakes and seas, they buy high and sell low; yet fortunately, their stolen goods have now been exposed, as I, an old monk, have broken through their camp.
If you still refuse to submit and remain unyielding, all travelers will be left beyond the green mountains.
Eulogy for Chan Master Dongyan Yunyang:
Clouds disperse across the vast sky; Warmth returns to the great earth. All sentient beings within the Flower Treasury World Draw their breath from the tip of the staff.
The Chan practitioner Yiyuan praises [the hermitage]:

"Even 'one' cannot be apprehended; where, then, can the traces of the hermitage remain? The precious pond is clear amidst vast surging waves, where a lotus-picking boat floats across. Master Guxin praises [it]: "Even 'one' is unattainable. Where could the traces of the hermitage persist? The jeweled pool is tranquil despite its great billows, as a lotus-harvesting boat is moored across it."
The ancient Buddhas have transmitted the lamp for long; the Master of Mind continues the flame far. If you wish to know where he has gone, look at the fragrant grasses lying in the slanting sun.
Venerable Layman Yu-zhai’s Eulogy (the layman shaved his head upon his death):
In such a state is this old man Yu-zhai: his beard and whiskers are white, yet not entirely white; he bears the appearance of a monk, yet is no mere form.
Let the ten-fascicle *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* circulate as you wish; let this single point of bodhi be subject to praise or slander.
Such a useless old dhūta as this has been banished into this most evil world of Jambudvīpa, left behind as a model for devas and humans.
To inscribe this thing upon silk as a self-praise is truly groundless; what is there to envy? It has shadow but no form, neither front nor back;
it has never been seen in heaven or among men. Its shadow is like the moon’s orb reflected in a thousand rivers; its form is like the Great [Void].
The lightning of emptiness is lovely; it reaches the subtle and knows the profound. It is loathsome; it leaks out myriad mechanisms and penetrates myriad transformations.
Sometimes it brings oneself to ruin; sometimes it deceives others. Tumbling and toppling, one fails to become a true person.
Do not wait until the King of Yama sees you! Why? Because in the end, it is difficult to prove that this is good.
Unwholesome! This fellow is unreasonable. First of all, he is not virtuous. He buries his head to eat and draws up his legs to sleep;
he neither aspires to the Way nor engages in Zen meditation. When someone encounters a priceless treasure, he says it is not worth half a cent. Even if there were...
When someone asked, "How is it? he suddenly struck him a punch to the chest. This was neither to deceive the earth nor to hoodwink heaven;
having encountered a true master, he immediately declared, "This is the separate transmission outside the teachings. Alas!
It may seem so, yet it is merely taking a horse for an ox—it does not know how to cultivate the fields of merit within the human world.
This old fellow is utterly deluded; he has not practiced the truth and merely engages in empty clamor.

He does not rely on the fundamental livelihoods of this world, but instead spends his time filling pits and digging holes in the mountains. Yet, though born in this land, he serves only the lineage of the Western Heaven’s Brahmā.
Throughout his life he was stubborn and disparaged the Chan school; yet he eventually gained the respect of the world’s gentlemen. Gradually, his ill repute spread in all directions.

Nevertheless, he did not fail his predecessors in succeeding to the Caodong lineage. Though in his lifetime he could not match the achievements of the various sages, in the end they shared the same nostril.
When he brandished his staff crosswise to strike others, the eyebrows of both saints and ordinary people ached at the mere sight or sound.
Do not concern yourself with him at all. Take care of yourselves. This old man is boundless;
that which cannot be known is now known. As soon as one engages in thought, it is like a silver mountain and an iron wall.
The empty *tathāgatagarbha* requires no effort; the barrier of the patriarchs is shattered without exertion. I shall now manifest this on a single sheet of paper—do not delay!
Those who reflect upon this will derive much benefit.
This fellow is most coarse; he has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake. He is unapproachable to people and takes no pleasure in seeing the Buddha.

Ordinarily, he merely flaps his tongue and wags his lips, claiming that "this very thing is it. Those who understand him will meet him with the staff until the end; those who do not understand will feign indifference and walk away.

In the rivers and lakes, there are many who give rise to anger. Those who do not act thus simply face the wall, remaining indifferent as they follow the flow of the world and pass their time, doing whatever is convenient for them.
Yet there are also those dull-witted fellows who insist on requesting paper [to write].
If they encounter a world-transcending *dhūta*, they will ultimately have their mouths twisted into a smile by him.
This old fellow—what merit does he possess? He troubles many people with his convoluted ways; this fellow is not even equal to empty space.
How could he have such a countenance? When pressed by others, he laughs heartily; when casually prodded, he is full of filth.

To questions about the wondrous, he answers with the mysterious, repeating himself three times and four ways. At times he speaks of iron walls and silver mountains; at other times he says that all is originally complete.
Some may show reverence to the sages and worthies, while others may offend the Buddhas and patriarchs. To include such unbalanced teachers among the ranks above—how could this be?
To take gold and adorn a wooden peg is clearly not what I call a field of merit.
Those who make offerings to me should fall into hell. Why is this? If a sweet melon is sweet all the way through to its stem, so too is the bitter gourd [bitter to its core].
This is bitter from root to tip. You clever monks, do not mock it!
This wretched old fellow has no skill at all; amidst the holy and the profane, he knows nothing of pain or pleasure.

He has lived among forests and springs for over forty years and has mixed with the worldly flow for nearly seventy. It was only upon reaching these great mountains that he finally recognized the Gate of the Patriarchs.

Turning his back [on convention], he traveled throughout the south and north to visit and seek instruction, discussing nothing but the single staff. He disregarded whether it was a sage or a demon approaching;
he personally executed the true command without negligence. He was perverse and did not conform to human sentiment;
he was arrogant and refused to tolerate comparison or measurement. To describe such a lackluster fellow as this—what use is there in copying his likeness?
This decrepit monk has exhausted every possible form and gesture. For twenty or thirty years atop solitary peaks, he captured the moon arising from the water;
for forty or fifty years wandering through various monasteries, he collided headlong with empty space.

He extinguished the lineage of the Barbarians, chanting to the moon and sighing to the wind; he shattered the school of Deva, seizing the clouds and riding the waves. Pushing sideways and sending straight ahead, he reduced everything to fragments.
The Patriarch’s Barrier: He beats down and drags away the empty *tathāgatagarbha*. I wonder what kind of skill he has learned to act so recklessly and arbitrarily?
I suspect he has mastered the regulations of a great mountain monastery, letting his mind run wild and unrestrained. (At the request of Baofang: What can this ignorant old man accomplish?
At fifty, he retired from the world to dwell among the forests and springs. Yet now we hear he has come crashing into Weikuan.

The Society. Thus, in the practice of meditation and liberation, one becomes deranged; one does not aspire for the sacred ground, nor does one cherish the field of the mind. Furthermore, there is no sense of taboo;

one is simply vacant and heedless, allowing the world’s suspicions to take their course as if one were unvirtuous. For the most part, neither the truly realized nor the ordinary can grasp such a person.

One shatters the three thousandfold and great thousandfold worlds, yet merely reveals oneself by saying, "My realization is not equal to that of the various sages. This occurs after the age of seventy.
Shangli Tian. Even regarding such matters of coming and going, there are those who write formal letters. This is because their minds are not settled in Chan.
*Du!* You are of the true lineage of Gautama; why do you not resemble his countenance? When discussing Chan, you are mostly vague and superficial;
when debating the teachings, you are entirely muddled. Your speech does not follow ancient rules, and your conduct lacks self-respect. Regarding the world...
There is not a single dharma that is long-lasting. How could one dare to receive the offerings of devas and humans?
This praise of the Perfect Circle (yuanxiang)—this segment of luminous wonder—is truly rare and precious. Among hundreds of thousands of devas and humans, only Kāśyapa broke into a smile.
Transmitted in succession from antiquity to the present, it has fortunately coincided with the circumstances of this humble mountain monk. Upon his thatched sickle he emits light;
by the side of his hoe he propagates the essential Dharma. He levels mountains and fills pitfalls to establish a site for practice; he hews stone and dams muddy pools to form irrigation channels.

He entices the monastics of the lakes and seas to risk their lives and sacrifice themselves, and commands the practitioners of the various mountains to hollow out their hearts and close off their worldly attachments.
Mouth. It is not that he is thus complete; how could he attain such coming and going? I have scribbled these lines in detail for Renzhen;
by all means, do not let a master understand them. Why? For fear that he would laugh without end. (At the request of Chen Yuanren and Yuanzhen of Shaxian:

To manifest the formless from within form, and to bring clarity to what is not yet clear—though Gu Kaizhi was a master of painting, it would be difficult for him to achieve this; only this wild monk is fit for it.
This is its reality. Therefore, it borrows a form to show it to people. If Master Bodhidharma were to see this, he would surely glare with wide-open eyes.
Why? Because he laughs at people; he laughs at people.
Such a thing—what is it like? It is round yet not round; it resembles radiance yet is not radiance. The Dharma-realm cannot contain it;
heaven and earth have no place to hold it. Unless one is a person who has realized their nature, it will ultimately be difficult to grasp.
